units.text: INT. RURAL RADIO STATION - NIGHT
A tin-roofed shack by a cornfield.
Foam-padded walls.
A glowing "ON AIR" sign.
A single microphone on a boom.
LORENZO BIANCHINI, 50s, in a bathrobe and headphones, leans back in a swivel chair and sips coffee.
Across the booth, FAYE OSTROWSKI, 20s, the board operator, scrolls through requests on a laptop.
IBRAHIM SESAY, 40s, a truck driver, sits on a stool by the door, waiting out the rain.
GRETA HALLSTROM, 60s, the station owner, knits in the corner.
It's two in the morning, and you're listening to Night Owl Radio. The rain is steady, the corn is quiet, and the phone lines are open.
units.name: LORENZO

units.text: You're good. Five more minutes and we can close.
units.name: FAYE

units.text: Can I stay until the rain stops?
units.name: IBRAHIM

units.text: You can stay until the pot runs out.
units.name: GRETA

units.text: The phone line rings.
Faye flips a switch.
Night Owl, you're on the air.
units.name: FAYE

units.text: Hello, Lorenzo. It's Marceline.
units.name: MARCELINE

units.text: Lorenzo's cup stops halfway to his mouth.
Greta's knitting needles go still.
Marceline. Hello.
units.name: LORENZO

units.text: I wanted to say thank you for the song last week.
units.name: MARCELINE

units.text: You're welcome.
units.name: LORENZO

units.text: I'm calling from the field behind the station. The corn is very tall tonight.
units.name: MARCELINE

units.text: Faye looks at the window.
Ibrahim stands.
Beyond the glass, rain and darkness and the black wall of corn.
That line is internal. There's no one out there.
units.name: FAYE

units.text: Lorenzo, would you play it again?
units.name: MARCELINE

units.text: Lorenzo sets down the cup.
He looks at Greta.
She nods, ashen.
Of course, Marceline. Anything for you.
units.name: LORENZO

units.text: He cues a record.
The needle drops.
Outside, something taps gently on the glass.
